+var (

+	relativePattern   = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\d+)\s*(second|minute|hour|day|week|month)s?\s*ago$`)
+)
+
+// ParseSinceAtNow parses durations like 7d, relative times like "2 days ago",
+// RFC3339 timestamps, and ISO dates.
+func ParseSinceAtNow(value string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
+	value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
+	if value == "" {
+		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unparseable --since: %q", value)
+	}
+
+	if matches := goDurationPattern.FindStringSubmatch(value); matches != nil {
+		n, err := strconv.Atoi(matches[1])
+		if err != nil {
+			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("parse duration count: %w", err)
+		}
+		switch matches[2] {
+		case "d":
+			return now.Add(-time.Duration(n) * 24 * time.Hour), nil
+		case "w":
+			return now.Add(-time.Duration(n) * 7 * 24 * time.Hour), nil
+		default:
+			d, err := time.ParseDuration(matches[1] + matches[2])
+			if err != nil {
+				return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("parse duration: %w", err)
+			}
+			return now.Add(-d), nil
+		}
+	}
+
+	if matches := relativePattern.FindStringSubmatch(strings.ToLower(value)); matches != nil {
+		n, err := strconv.Atoi(matches[1])
+		if err != nil {
+			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("parse relative count: %w", err)
+		}
+		var unit time.Duration
+		switch matches[2] {
+		case "second":
+			unit = time.Second
+		case "minute":
+			unit = time.Minute
+		case "hour":
+			unit = time.Hour
+		case "day":
+			unit = 24 * time.Hour
+		case "week":
+			unit = 7 * 24 * time.Hour
+		case "month":
+			unit = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+		}
+		return now.Add(-time.Duration(n) * unit), nil
+	}
+
+	if parsed, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, value); err == nil {
+		return parsed, nil
+	}
+	if parsed, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02", value); err == nil {
+		return parsed, nil
+	}
+
+	return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unparseable --since: %q", value)

I’m reading the checkpoint/test utilities now so the local-mode test setup is realistic and isolated.

I’m inserting the fallback chain before local mode. That keeps the local runner thin: enumerate checkpoints, fetch analyses, then hand each checkpoint through one straight-line resolver instead of duplicating status logic in the runner itself.

+package cli
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+
+	dispatchpkg "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/dispatch"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+func newDispatchCmd() *cobra.Command {
+	var (
+		flagLocal    bool
+		flagSince    string
+		flagUntil    string
+		flagBranches string
+		flagRepos    []string
+		flagOrg      string
+		flagGenerate bool
+		flagVoice    string
+		flagFormat   string
+		flagDryRun   bool
+		flagWait     bool
+	)
+
+	cmd := &cobra.Command{
+		Use:   "dispatch",
+		Short: "Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work",
+		Long: `Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work.
+
+Examples:
+  entire dispatch
+  entire dispatch --since 14d --branches main,release
+  entire dispatch --local --repos ~/Projects/cli
+  entire dispatch --format markdown
+  entire dispatch --generate --voice neutral`,
+		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
+			opts, err := parseDispatchFlags(cmd, flagLocal, flagSince, flagUntil, flagBranches, flagRepos, flagOrg, flagGenerate, flagVoice, flagFormat, flagDryRun, flagWait)
+			if err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+
+			result, err := dispatchpkg.Run(cmd.Context(), opts)
+			if err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+
+			rendered, err := dispatchpkg.Render(opts.Format, result)
+			if err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+			fmt.Fprint(cmd.OutOrStdout(), rendered)
+			if opts.Format != "json" && result.WebURL != "" {
+				fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "\n%s\n", result.WebURL)
+			}
+			return nil
+		},
+	}
+
+	cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flagLocal, "local", false, "use local LLM tokens instead of server synthesis")
+	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&flagSince, "since", "7d", "time window (Go duration, relative time, or ISO date)")
+	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&flagUntil, "until", "", "window end time (defaults to now)")
+	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&flagBranches, "branches", "", "comma-separated branch names, or 'all'")
+	cmd.Flags().StringSliceVar(&flagRepos, "repos", nil, "local repo paths (requires --local)")
+	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&flagOrg, "org", "", "enumerate checkpoints across an org")
+	cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flagGenerate, "generate", false, "synthesize prose from dispatch bullets")
+	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&flagVoice, "voice", "", "voice preset name, file path, or literal description")
+	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&flagFormat, "format", "text", "output format: text | markdown | json")
+	cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flagDryRun, "dry-run", false, "preview without persisting")
+	cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flagWait, "wait", false, "wait for pending analyses to complete")
+
+	return cmd
+}
+
+func parseDispatchFlags(
+	cmd *cobra.Command,
+	flagLocal bool,
+	flagSince string,
+	flagUntil string,
+	flagBranches string,
+	flagRepos []string,
+	flagOrg string,
+	flagGenerate bool,
+	flagVoice string,
+	flagFormat string,
+	flagDryRun bool,
+	flagWait bool,
+) (dispatchpkg.Options, error) {
+	if flagOrg != "" && len(flagRepos) > 0 {
+		return dispatchpkg.Options{}, errors.New("--org and --repos are mutually exclusive")
+	}
+	if !flagLocal && len(flagRepos) > 0 {
+		return dispatchpkg.Options{}, errors.New("--repos requires --local")
+	}
+
+	format := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(flagFormat))
+	switch format {
+	case "", "text":
+		format = "text"
+	case "markdown", "json":
+	default:
+		return dispatchpkg.Options{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported format %q", flagFormat)
+	}
+
+	mode := dispatchpkg.ModeServer
+	if flagLocal {
+		mode = dispatchpkg.ModeLocal
+	}
+
+	branches, allBranches, err := dispatchpkg.ParseBranches(flagBranches, "")
+	if err != nil {
+		return dispatchpkg.Options{}, err
+	}
+	if !allBranches && len(branches) == 1 && branches[0] == "" && len(flagRepos) == 0 {
+		currentBranch, branchErr := GetCurrentBranch(cmd.Context())
+		if branchErr != nil {
+			return dispatchpkg.Options{}, branchErr
+		}
+		branches = []string{currentBranch}
+	}
+
+	return dispatchpkg.Options{
+		Mode:        mode,
+		RepoPaths:   append([]string(nil), flagRepos...),
+		Org:         flagOrg,
+		Since:       flagSince,
+		Until:       flagUntil,
+		Branches:    branches,
+		AllBranches: allBranches,

+
+func runDispatchWizard(cmd *cobra.Command) (dispatchpkg.Options, error) {
+	var (
+		modeChoice string
+		since      = "7d"
+		branches   string
+		org        string
+		reposCSV   string
+		generate   bool
+		voice      string
+		format     = "text"
+		dryRun     bool
+		wait       bool
+	)
+
+	form := NewAccessibleForm(
+		huh.NewGroup(
+			huh.NewSelect[string]().
+				Title("Dispatch mode").
+				Options(
+					huh.NewOption("Server", "server"),
+					huh.NewOption("Local", "local"),
+				).
+				Value(&modeChoice),
+			huh.NewInput().
+				Title("Since").
+				Description("Examples: 7d, 2 days ago, 2026-04-09").
+				Value(&since),
+			huh.NewInput().
+				Title("Branches").
+				Description("Comma-separated branch names, or 'all'. Leave blank for current branch.").
+				Value(&branches),
+			huh.NewInput().
+				Title("Org").
+				Description("Optional org-wide dispatch scope. Leave blank for current repo.").
+				Value(&org),
+			huh.NewInput().
+				Title("Repos").
+				Description("Optional local repo paths, comma-separated. Requires local mode.").
+				Value(&reposCSV),
+			huh.NewConfirm().
+				Title("Generate prose?").
+				Value(&generate),
+			huh.NewInput().
+				Title("Voice").
+				Description("Preset name, file path, or literal guidance. Leave blank for neutral.").
+				Value(&voice),
+			huh.NewSelect[string]().
+				Title("Format").
+				Options(
+					huh.NewOption("Text", "text"),
+					huh.NewOption("Markdown", "markdown"),
+					huh.NewOption("JSON", "json"),
+				).
+				Value(&format),
+			huh.NewConfirm().
+				Title("Dry run?").
+				Value(&dryRun),
+			huh.NewConfirm().
+				Title("Wait for pending analyses?").
+				Value(&wait),
+		),
+	)
+	if err := form.Run(); err != nil {
+		return dispatchpkg.Options{}, handleFormCancellation(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "dispatch", err)
+	}
+
+	var repos []string
+	if strings.TrimSpace(reposCSV) != "" {
+		for _, repo := range strings.Split(reposCSV, ",") {

+				repos = append(repos, repo)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+
+	return parseDispatchFlags(

+		since,

+		branches,
+		repos,
+		org,

+    since,
+    new Date(normalizedUntil.getTime() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000),
+  )
+
+  return {
+    normalized_since: normalizedSince.toISOString(),
+    normalized_until: normalizedUntil.toISOString(),
+    first_checkpoint_created_at: null,
+    last_checkpoint_created_at: null,
+  }
+}
+
+function isCheckpointInWindow(checkpoint: CheckpointWithCommit, window: DispatchWindow): boolean {
+  const timestamp = checkpoint.created_at ?? checkpoint.commit_date
+  if (!timestamp) return true
+
+  const createdAt = new Date(timestamp).getTime()
+  if (Number.isNaN(createdAt)) return true
+
+  return (
+    createdAt >= new Date(window.normalized_since).getTime() &&
+    createdAt <= new Date(window.normalized_until).getTime()
+  )
+}
+
+function parseStoredCheckpointAnalysis(analysisJson: string | null): StoredCheckpointAnalysis | null {
+  if (!analysisJson) return null
+
+  try {
+    return JSON.parse(analysisJson) as StoredCheckpointAnalysis
+  } catch {
+    return null
+  }
+}
+
+function blockSummary(block: ExtractionBlock): string | null {
+  const candidates = [
+    block.narrative,
+    block.accepted,
+    block.reasoning,
+    block.keyFindings?.[0],
+    block.openQuestions?.[0],
+    block.title,
+  ]
+
+  for (const candidate of candidates) {
+    if (typeof candidate === "string" && candidate.trim()) {
+      return candidate.trim()
+    }
+  }
+
+  return null
+}
+
+function titleCaseBlockType(type: ExtractionBlock["type"]): string {
+  return type.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + type.slice(1)
+}
+
+function extractCheckpointSections(
+  checkpoint: CheckpointWithCommit,
+  analysis: AnalysisRow | undefined,
+): {
+  sections: DispatchSection[]
+  usedCheckpoint: boolean
+  fallbackUsed: boolean
+  warningCounts: Partial<DispatchWarnings>
+} {
+  const warningCounts: Partial<DispatchWarnings> = {}
+
+  if (!analysis) {
+    warningCounts.unknown_count = 1
+  } else if (analysis.status === "pending" || analysis.status === "generating") {
+    warningCounts.pending_count = 1
+  } else if (analysis.status === "failed") {
+    warningCounts.failed_count = 1
+  }
+
+  const parsedAnalysis =
+    analysis?.status === "complete" ? parseStoredCheckpointAnalysis(analysis.analysis_json) : null
+  const labels = parsedAnalysis?.extraction.labels ?? []
+  const blocks = parsedAnalysis?.extraction.blocks ?? []
+
+  if (blocks.length > 0) {
+    const sections = new Map<string, DispatchBullet[]>()
+
+    for (const block of blocks) {
+      const text = blockSummary(block)
+      if (!text) continue
+
+      const label = titleCaseBlockType(block.type)
+      const bullet: DispatchBullet = {
+        checkpoint_id: checkpoint.checkpoint_id,
+        text,
+        source: "cloud_analysis",
+        branch: checkpoint.branch ?? "unknown",
+        created_at: checkpoint.created_at ?? checkpoint.commit_date ?? new Date().toISOString(),
+        labels,
+      }
+      const current = sections.get(label) ?? []
+      current.push(bullet)
+      sections.set(label, current)
+    }
+
+    if (sections.size > 0) {
+      return {
+        sections: [...sections.entries()].map(([label, bullets]) => ({ label, bullets })),
+        usedCheckpoint: true,
+        fallbackUsed: false,
+        warningCounts,
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  const fallbackText = checkpoint.commit_message?.trim() || checkpoint.prompt?.trim()
+  if (!fallbackText) {
+    return {
+      sections: [],
+      usedCheckpoint: false,
+      fallbackUsed: false,
+      warningCounts: { ...warningCounts, uncategorized_count: 1 },
+    }
+  }
+
+  return {
+    sections: [
+      {
+        label: "Highlights",
+        bullets: [
+          {
+            checkpoint_id: checkpoint.checkpoint_id,
+            text: fallbackText,
+            source: "commit_message",
+            branch: checkpoint.branch ?? "unknown",
+            created_at: checkpoint.created_at ?? checkpoint.commit_date ?? new Date().toISOString(),
+            labels,
+          },
+        ],
+      },
+    ],
+    usedCheckpoint: true,
+    fallbackUsed: true,
+    warningCounts,
+  }
+}
+
+function mergeWarnings(target: DispatchWarnings, source: Partial<DispatchWarnings>): void {
+  for (const key of Object.keys(source) as Array<keyof DispatchWarnings>) {
+    target[key] += source[key] ?? 0
+  }
+}
+
+function buildGeneratedMarkdown(title: string, repos: DispatchRepoGroup[]): string {
+  const lines: string[] = [`# ${title}`]
+
+  for (const repo of repos) {
+    lines.push("", `## ${repo.full_name}`)
+    for (const section of repo.sections) {
+      lines.push("", `### ${section.label}`)
+      for (const bullet of section.bullets) {
+        lines.push(`- ${bullet.text}`)
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  return lines.join("\n").trim()
+}
+
+function buildGeneratedText(repos: DispatchRepoGroup[]): string {
+  const lines: string[] = []
+
+  for (const repo of repos) {
+    lines.push(repo.full_name)
+    for (const section of repo.sections) {
+      lines.push(`${section.label}:`)
+      for (const bullet of section.bullets) {
+        lines.push(`- ${bullet.text}`)
+      }
+    }
+    lines.push("")
+  }
+
+  return lines.join("\n").trim()
+}
+
+function buildExcerpt(markdown: string): string {
+  const content = markdown
+    .replace(/^#+\s+/gm, "")
+    .replace(/^\-\s+/gm, "")
+    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
+    .trim()
+
+  return content.slice(0, 180)
+}
+
+function summarizeTitle(scopeRepo: string | null, scopeOrg: string | null, repoCount: number): string {
+  if (scopeRepo) return `Dispatch for ${scopeRepo}`
+  if (scopeOrg) return `Dispatch for ${scopeOrg}`
+  if (repoCount === 1) return "Dispatch"
+  return `Dispatch across ${repoCount} repos`
+}
+
+function determineStatus(
+  warnings: DispatchWarnings,
+  usedCheckpointCount: number,
+): DispatchStatus {
+  if (warnings.pending_count > 0) return "generating"
+  if (warnings.failed_count > 0 && usedCheckpointCount === 0) return "failed"
+  return "complete"
+}

+async function resolveRepoBranches(
+  db: Db,
+  repoId: string,
+  defaultBranch: string,
+  requestedBranches: DispatchBranches | undefined,
+): Promise<string[]> {
+  if (requestedBranches === "all") {
+    const branches = await db.checkpoints.getBranchesWithCheckpoints(repoId)
+    return [...new Set(branches.map((branch) => branch.branch).filter(Boolean))]
+  }
+
+  if (!requestedBranches || requestedBranches.length === 0) {
+    return [defaultBranch]
+  }
+
+  return [...new Set(requestedBranches.map((branch) => branch.trim()).filter(Boolean))]
+}
+
+async function collectRepoDispatchData(
+  db: Db,
+  userId: string,
+  repo: Awaited<ReturnType<Db["repos"]["getByFullName"]>>,
+  requestedBranches: DispatchBranches | undefined,
+  window: DispatchWindow,
+): Promise<RepoDispatchData | null> {
+  if (!repo) return null
+
+  const selectedBranches = await resolveRepoBranches(
+    db,
+    repo.id,
+    repo.default_branch || "main",
+    requestedBranches,
+  )
+
+  const branchResults = await Promise.all(
+    selectedBranches.map((branch) => db.checkpoints.getRepoWithCheckpoints(repo.full_name, userId, branch, 100)),
+  )
+
+  const checkpointMap = new Map<string, CheckpointWithCommit>()
+  for (const result of branchResults) {
+    if (!result || result === "no_access") continue
+    for (const checkpoint of result.checkpoints) {
+      if (!isCheckpointInWindow(checkpoint, window)) continue
+      if (!checkpointMap.has(checkpoint.checkpoint_id)) {
+        checkpointMap.set(checkpoint.checkpoint_id, checkpoint)
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  const checkpoints = [...checkpointMap.values()].sort((left, right) => {
+    const leftTime = new Date(left.created_at ?? left.commit_date ?? 0).getTime()
+    const rightTime = new Date(right.created_at ?? right.commit_date ?? 0).getTime()
+    return rightTime - leftTime
+  })
+
+  const analyses = checkpoints.length
+    ? await db.analyses.getByCheckpointIds(
+        repo.id,
+        checkpoints.map((checkpoint) => checkpoint.checkpoint_id),
+      )
+    : []
+  const analysesByCheckpointId = new Map(analyses.map((analysis) => [analysis.checkpoint_id, analysis]))
+
+  const warnings = emptyWarnings()
+  const sections = new Map<string, DispatchBullet[]>()
+  const filesTouched = new Set<string>()
+  let usedCheckpointCount = 0
+
+  for (const checkpoint of checkpoints) {
+    for (const file of checkpoint.files_touched ?? []) {
+      filesTouched.add(file)
+    }
+
+    const result = extractCheckpointSections(
+      checkpoint,
+      analysesByCheckpointId.get(checkpoint.checkpoint_id),
+    )
+    mergeWarnings(warnings, result.warningCounts)
+    if (result.usedCheckpoint) {
+      usedCheckpointCount += 1
+    }
+
+    for (const section of result.sections) {
+      const current = sections.get(section.label) ?? []
+      current.push(...section.bullets)
+      sections.set(section.label, current)
+    }
+  }
+
+  return {
+    fullName: repo.full_name,
+    checkpoints,
+    selectedBranches,
+    sections: [...sections.entries()].map(([label, bullets]) => ({ label, bullets })),
+    warnings,
+    usedCheckpointCount,
+    filesTouched,
+  }
+}

+async function buildDispatchRecord(
+  db: Db,
+  userId: string,
+  body: CreateDispatchRequest,
+): Promise<DispatchRecord | null> {
+  const scopeRepo = body.repo?.trim() || null
+  const scopeOrg = body.org?.trim() || null
+
+  if (!scopeRepo && !scopeOrg) {
+    return null
+  }
+
+  const window = normalizeWindow(body.since, body.until)
+  const repoNames =
+    scopeRepo !== null
+      ? [scopeRepo]
+      : (await db.repos.getAccessibleByUser(userId))
+          .filter((repo) => repo.full_name.startsWith(`${scopeOrg}/`))
+          .map((repo) => repo.full_name)
+
+  const repos = await Promise.all(repoNames.map((repoName) => db.repos.getByFullName(repoName)))
+  const repoData = (
+    await Promise.all(
+      repos.map((repo) => collectRepoDispatchData(db, userId, repo, body.branches, window)),
+    )
+  ).filter((repo): repo is RepoDispatchData => repo !== null)
+
+  const coveredRepos = repoData.map((repo) => repo.fullName)
+  const allBranches = [...new Set(repoData.flatMap((repo) => repo.selectedBranches))]
+  const warnings = emptyWarnings()
+  const filesTouched = new Set<string>()
+  const checkpointTimestamps: string[] = []
+
+  for (const repo of repoData) {
+    mergeWarnings(warnings, repo.warnings)
+    for (const file of repo.filesTouched) {
+      filesTouched.add(file)
+    }
+    for (const checkpoint of repo.checkpoints) {
+      const timestamp = checkpoint.created_at ?? checkpoint.commit_date
+      if (timestamp) checkpointTimestamps.push(timestamp)
+    }
+  }
+
+  checkpointTimestamps.sort((left, right) => new Date(left).getTime() - new Date(right).getTime())
+  window.first_checkpoint_created_at = checkpointTimestamps[0] ?? null
+  window.last_checkpoint_created_at = checkpointTimestamps.at(-1) ?? null
+
+  const repoGroups: DispatchRepoGroup[] = repoData.map((repo) => ({
+    full_name: repo.fullName,
+    sections: repo.sections,
+  }))
+  const usedCheckpointCount = repoData.reduce((sum, repo) => sum + repo.usedCheckpointCount, 0)
+  const title = summarizeTitle(scopeRepo, scopeOrg, repoGroups.length)
+  const generatedMarkdown = buildGeneratedMarkdown(title, repoGroups)
+  const generatedText = buildGeneratedText(repoGroups)
+  const generatedAt = new Date().toISOString()
+  const totals: DispatchTotals = {
+    checkpoints: repoData.reduce((sum, repo) => sum + repo.checkpoints.length, 0),
+    used_checkpoint_count: usedCheckpointCount,
+    branches: allBranches.length,
+    files_touched: filesTouched.size,
+  }
+
+  const detail: DispatchDetail = {
+    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
+    title,
+    excerpt: buildExcerpt(generatedMarkdown),
+    status: determineStatus(warnings, usedCheckpointCount),
+    covered_repos: coveredRepos,
+    voice: body.voice?.trim() || null,
+    generated_at: generatedAt,
+    window,
+    totals,
+    fingerprint_hash: null,
+    branches: body.branches === "all" ? "all" : allBranches,
+    web_url: null,
+    generated_markdown: generatedMarkdown,
+    generated_text: generatedText || null,
+    repos: repoGroups,
+    warnings,
+  }
+
+  return {
+    ...detail,
+    user_id: userId,
+    scope: {
+      repo: scopeRepo,
+      org: scopeOrg,
+    },
+    generated_text_search: `${detail.title}\n${detail.excerpt}\n${detail.generated_markdown}`.toLowerCase(),
+  }
+}
+
+function matchesListFilters(
+  record: DispatchRecord,
+  params: URLSearchParams,
+  scope: { repo?: string; org?: string },
+): boolean {
+  if (scope.repo && !record.covered_repos.includes(scope.repo)) return false
+  if (scope.org && !record.covered_repos.some((repo) => repo.startsWith(`${scope.org}/`))) return false
+
+  const voice = params.get("voice")?.trim().toLowerCase()
+  if (voice && (record.voice ?? "").toLowerCase() !== voice) return false
+
+  const query = params.get("q")?.trim().toLowerCase()
+  if (query && !record.generated_text_search.includes(query)) return false
+
+  const since = params.get("since")
+  if (since) {
+    const sinceDate = parseTimeInput(since, new Date())
+    if (new Date(record.generated_at).getTime() < sinceDate.getTime()) return false
+  }
+
+  const until = params.get("until")
+  if (until) {

+    if (new Date(record.generated_at).getTime() > untilDate.getTime()) return false
+  }

In `entire.io`, I added authenticated dispatch endpoints in [dispatches.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/routes/dispatches.ts:1) and mounted them in [app.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/app.ts:1), with route coverage in [dispatches.test.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/routes/dispatches.test.ts:1). The create page in [DispatchNewPage.tsx](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/frontend/src/domains/platform/dispatches/pages/DispatchNewPage.tsx:1) now sends empty branch arrays for “Default” instead of coercing to `"all"`, and the backend resolves that to each repo’s default branch. I removed the CLI affordance entirely by deleting [OpenInCliModal.tsx](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/frontend/src/domains/platform/dispatches/components/OpenInCliModal.tsx:1), removing sidebar wiring in [DispatchSidebar.tsx](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/frontend/src/domains/platform/dispatches/components/DispatchSidebar.tsx:1), and dropping the preview-side CLI block in [DispatchPreviewPane.tsx](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/frontend/src/domains/platform/dispatches/components/DispatchPreviewPane.tsx:1). The detail page in [DispatchDetailPage.tsx](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/frontend/src/domains/platform/dispatches/pages/DispatchDetailPage.tsx:1) now has explicit `generating` and `failed` states, and the preview pane now shows repos, branches, window, checkpoint count, used checkpoint count, and files touched.

In the CLI repo, [dispatch.go](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/cmd/entire/cli/dispatch.go:1) now only launches the wizard when both stdin and stdout are terminals, and the wizard defaults `Generate prose?` to `true`. I added focused coverage in [dispatch_test.go](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_test.go:1).

Verification:

- `pnpm run frontend:build` in `entire.io` passed
- `pnpm run lint` in `entire.io` passed with the same 9 pre-existing warnings in unrelated files
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/dispatch ./cmd/entire/cli` passed

content.text:
Not fully to spec.

**Findings**
1. The backend authorization model is still wrong. The spec requires shared dispatches with live repo-access checks for every viewer, but the implementation stores `user_id`, keeps a per-user KV index, and only allows detail fetches when `record.user_id === userId`. That makes dispatches owner-scoped instead of content-addressed shared objects, and it never re-authorizes `covered_repos` on detail fetch. See [dispatches.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/routes/dispatches.ts:77), [dispatches.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/routes/dispatches.ts:114), [dispatches.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/routes/dispatches.ts:655), and [dispatches.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/routes/dispatches.ts:684). This violates the web spec’s access-control model at [2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-web-ui-design.md](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-web-ui-design.md:35).

2. `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` does not match the persistence/idempotency contract. The route persists any non-dry-run request regardless of `generate`, always returns the persisted-style fields, always assigns a fresh UUID, and never computes a fingerprint or dedupe result. `generate: false` is supposed to be non-persisted inline output, and `generate: true` is supposed to dedupe on the content-addressed fingerprint. See [dispatches.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/routes/dispatches.ts:555), [dispatches.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/routes/dispatches.ts:655), and [dispatches.ts](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/dispatch-web-ui-codex/api/src/routes/dispatches.ts:663). This conflicts with the API contract at [2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-web-ui-design.md](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-web-ui-design.md:218).

3. The repo/org list endpoints do not apply the required per-dispatch authorization filter. +# Dispatch Bubble Tea TUI Design
+
+**Date:** 2026-04-17
+**Status:** Approved
+
+## Goal
+
+Replace the current `huh`-based `entire dispatch` wizard with a Bubble Tea TUI that matches the repo's existing interactive CLI patterns and provides a live local preview of the resolved dispatch options.
+
+## Context
+
+The current dispatch wizard lives inline in `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch.go` and is implemented as one large `huh` form. That is inconsistent with the rest of the repo's richer interactive command surface, where `entire search` uses Bubble Tea, Lip Gloss, and a dedicated TUI model with tests.
+
+This rewrite is intentionally narrow:
+
+- Keep the existing dispatch execution path intact.
+- Replace only the interactive input collection path.
+- Preserve non-interactive flag parsing and output rendering.
+- Preserve accessible mode by keeping a linear prompt fallback instead of forcing Bubble Tea there.
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Auto-launch only when `entire dispatch` is run with no explicit flags and both stdin/stdout are terminals.
+- Skip the TUI for piped stdin, non-terminal stdout, or any explicit flags.
+- Skip Bubble Tea entirely in `ACCESSIBLE=1` and use a simple accessible prompt path.
+- Match repo conventions established by `entire search`:
+  - `tea.NewProgram(..., tea.WithAltScreen())`
+  - dedicated model and tests
+  - Lip Gloss styling based on repo palette
+- Show a live preview that is purely local:
+  - effective mode
+  - effective scope
+  - effective branch behavior
+  - exact command preview
+  - validation errors
+- Do not run dispatch work inside the TUI loop.
+- Return collected values to the existing parse/execute path.
+
+## Interaction Model
+
+The TUI is a single-screen two-pane wizard.
+
+- Header:
+  - `DISPATCH` title
+  - current interaction mode
+  - brief description
+- Left pane:
+  - editable fields in a fixed order
+  - one focused field at a time
+  - navigation mode vs text editing mode
+- Right pane:
+  - live summary of resolved options
+  - validation errors
+  - exact command that would run
+- Footer:
+  - key legend for navigation, editing, submit, and quit
+
+## Fields
+
+The left pane collects the same inputs currently handled by the old wizard:
+
+1. Mode: server or local
+2. Since
+3. Until
+4. Branch scope: default, all, custom
+5. Custom branches
+6. Org
+7. Repos
+8. Generate
+9. Voice
+10. Format
+11. Dry run
+12. Wait
+
+## Preview Behavior
+
+The preview is derived from local state only.
+
+- No network calls
+- No dry-run dispatch execution
+- No checkpoint enumeration
+
+It computes the same defaults as `parseDispatchFlags`:
+
+- current branch fallback for repo mode without explicit branches
+- org mode defaults to all branches
+- local `--repos` requires local mode
+- `--org` and `--repos` are mutually exclusive
+- output format defaults and validation match the existing parser
+
+The preview shows raw user text in editable fields, but derived values in the summary. Normalization happens in preview computation rather than rewriting the field state during editing.
+
+## Architecture
+
+The Bubble Tea layer is input collection only.
+
+- `newDispatchCmd()` still owns top-level command behavior.
+- `parseDispatchFlags(...)` remains the source of truth for the final `dispatchpkg.Options`.
+- A new `runDispatchTUI(cmd *cobra.Command) (dispatchpkg.Options, error)` replaces `runDispatchWizard(...)` for interactive terminals.
+- The TUI returns collected raw values, which are then passed through existing parsing/validation logic.
+- `dispatchpkg.Run(...)` and rendering stay unchanged.
+
+## State Model
+
+Top-level model fields:
+
+- terminal width/height
+- focus index
+- interaction mode (`navigate`, `edit`, `confirm`)
+- per-field state
+- derived preview state
+- submission/cancel result
+- error string
+
+Text fields use `bubbles/textinput`. Enum and boolean fields are rendered with repo-consistent key-driven toggles.
+
+## Accessibility
+
+Accessible mode remains outside Bubble Tea.
+
+- If `ACCESSIBLE=1`, the command uses a simple linear prompt flow.
+- That keeps compatibility with the repo's existing accessibility contract.
+- The Bubble Tea path is only for fully interactive terminal users.
+
+## Testing Strategy
+
+Add Bubble Tea model tests parallel to `search_tui_test.go`.
+
+Primary coverage:
+
+- default preview resolves current branch in repo mode
+- org mode resolves to all branches
+- local repos on server mode produce validation error
+- submit returns collected values
+- quit cancels cleanly
+- command launch conditions still skip TUI when flags are provided or stdin is piped
+- accessible mode uses the fallback path
+
+## File Layout
+
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch.go`
+  - command wiring
+  - TUI launch decision
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_tui.go`
+  - Bubble Tea model, update, and view
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_tui_test.go`
+  - model tests
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_accessible.go`
+  - accessible prompt fallback
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_test.go`
+  - command entry and launch-condition tests
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- No server-backed preview
+- No checkpoint enumeration inside the TUI
+- No persistence of partially completed wizard state
+- No modal multi-step flow
+- No changes to dispatch output formats or backend request behavior

+func (m dispatchTUIModel) activeInput() *textinput.Model {
+	switch m.focusIndex {

+func (m *dispatchTUIModel) formatActiveInput() {
+	for _, input := range []*textinput.Model{&m.sinceInput, &m.untilInput, &m.branchesInput, &m.orgInput, &m.reposInput, &m.voiceInput} {
+		input.Blur()

+
+func (m dispatchTUIModel) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) { //nolint:ireturn
+	switch msg := msg.(type) {
+	case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
+		m.width = msg.Width
+		m.height = msg.Height
+		return m, nil
+	case tea.KeyMsg:
+		if m.interaction == dispatchTUIInteractionEdit {
+			return m.updateEditMode(msg)
+		}
+		return m.updateNavigateMode(msg)
+	}
+	return m, nil
+}
+
+func (m dispatchTUIModel) updateEditMode(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) { //nolint:ireturn
+	switch msg.String() {
+	case "esc", "enter":
+		m.interaction = dispatchTUIInteractionNavigate
+		m.formatActiveInput()
+		return m, nil
+	case "ctrl+c":
+		m.cancelled = true
+		return m, tea.Quit
+	}
+
+	input := m.activeInput()
+	if input == nil {
+		m.interaction = dispatchTUIInteractionNavigate
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	updated, cmd := input.Update(msg)
+	*input = updated
+	return m, cmd
+}
+
+func (m dispatchTUIModel) updateNavigateMode(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) { //nolint:ireturn,cyclop
+	switch msg.String() {
+	case "ctrl+c", "q", "esc":
+		m.cancelled = true
+		return m, tea.Quit
+	case "tab", "down", "j":
+		m.focusIndex = (m.focusIndex + 1) % dispatchTUIFieldCount
+		return m, nil
+	case "shift+tab", "up", "k":
+		m.focusIndex = (m.focusIndex + dispatchTUIFieldCount - 1) % dispatchTUIFieldCount
+		return m, nil
+	case "left", "h":
+		m.adjustFocusedField(-1)
+		return m, nil
+	case "right", "l", " ":
+		m.adjustFocusedField(1)
+		return m, nil
+	case "enter":
+		if m.activeInput() != nil {
+			m.interaction = dispatchTUIInteractionEdit
+			m.formatActiveInput()
+		} else {
+			m.adjustFocusedField(1)
+		}
+		return m, nil
+	case "r":
+		preview := m.preview()
+		if preview.ValidationError != "" {
+			return m, nil
+		}
+		m.submitted = true
+		m.submittedOpts = preview.Options
+		return m, tea.Quit
+	}
+	return m, nil
+}

+func (m *dispatchTUIModel) adjustFocusedField(direction int) {
+	switch m.focusIndex {
+	case dispatchTUIFieldSource:
+		if direction > 0 {
+			if m.sourceMode == dispatchTUISourceModeServer {
+				m.sourceMode = dispatchTUISourceModeLocal
+			} else {
+				m.sourceMode = dispatchTUISourceModeServer
+			}
+		} else {
+			if m.sourceMode == dispatchTUISourceModeLocal {
+				m.sourceMode = dispatchTUISourceModeServer
+			} else {
+				m.sourceMode = dispatchTUISourceModeLocal
+			}
+		}
+	case dispatchTUIFieldBranchScope:
+		switch m.branchMode {
+		case dispatchTUIBranchModeDefault:
+			if direction > 0 {
+				m.branchMode = dispatchTUIBranchModeAll
+			} else {
+				m.branchMode = dispatchTUIBranchModeCustom
+			}
+		case dispatchTUIBranchModeAll:
+			if direction > 0 {
+				m.branchMode = dispatchTUIBranchModeCustom
+			} else {
+				m.branchMode = dispatchTUIBranchModeDefault
+			}
+		case dispatchTUIBranchModeCustom:
+			if direction > 0 {
+				m.branchMode = dispatchTUIBranchModeDefault
+			} else {
+				m.branchMode = dispatchTUIBranchModeAll
+			}
+		}
+	case dispatchTUIFieldGenerate:
+		m.generate = !m.generate
+	case dispatchTUIFieldFormat:
+		formats := []string{"text", "markdown", "json"}
+		idx := 0
+		for i, format := range formats {
+			if format == m.format {
+				idx = i
+				break
+			}
+		}
+		idx = (idx + direction + len(formats)) % len(formats)
+		m.format = formats[idx]
+	case dispatchTUIFieldDryRun:
+		m.dryRun = !m.dryRun
+	case dispatchTUIFieldWait:
+		m.wait = !m.wait
+	}
+}

+func (m dispatchTUIModel) preview() dispatchTUIPreview {
+	branchesFlag := ""
+	switch m.branchMode {
+	case dispatchTUIBranchModeAll:
+		branchesFlag = "all"
+	case dispatchTUIBranchModeCustom:
+		branchesFlag = m.branchesInput.Value()
+	}
+
+	opts, err := resolveDispatchOptions(
+		m.sourceMode == dispatchTUISourceModeLocal,
+		m.sinceInput.Value(),
+		m.untilInput.Value(),
+		branchesFlag,
+		splitCSVField(m.reposInput.Value()),
+		strings.TrimSpace(m.orgInput.Value()),
+		m.generate,
+		strings.TrimSpace(m.voiceInput.Value()),
+		m.format,
+		m.dryRun,
+		m.wait,
+		m.currentBranch,
+	)
+	if err != nil {
+		return dispatchTUIPreview{
+			ValidationError: err.Error(),
+			EffectiveMode:   m.sourceMode.label(),
+			EffectiveScope:  m.previewScope(),
+			Command:         m.previewCommandFromRaw(branchesFlag),
+		}
+	}
+
+	effectiveBranches := "current branch"
+	if opts.AllBranches {
+		effectiveBranches = "all"
+	} else if len(opts.Branches) > 0 {
+		effectiveBranches = strings.Join(opts.Branches, ",")
+	}
+
+	return dispatchTUIPreview{
+		EffectiveMode:    m.sourceMode.label(),
+		EffectiveScope:   m.previewScope(),
+		EffectiveBranches: effectiveBranches,
+		Command:          buildDispatchCommand(opts),
+		Options:          opts,
+	}
+}

+func (m dispatchTUIModel) previewScope() string {
+	org := strings.TrimSpace(m.orgInput.Value())
+	repos := splitCSVField(m.reposInput.Value())
+	switch {
+	case org != "":
+		return "org:" + org
+	case len(repos) > 0:
+		return "repos:" + strings.Join(repos, ",")
+	default:
+		return "current repo"
+	}
+}

+func (m dispatchTUIModel) previewCommandFromRaw(branchesFlag string) string {
+	return strings.Join(compactStrings([]string{
+		"entire dispatch",
+		mapBoolToFlag(m.sourceMode == dispatchTUISourceModeLocal, "--local"),
+		renderStringFlag("--since", strings.TrimSpace(m.sinceInput.Value())),
+		renderStringFlag("--until", strings.TrimSpace(m.untilInput.Value())),
+		renderStringFlag("--branches", strings.TrimSpace(branchesFlag)),
+		renderStringFlag("--org", strings.TrimSpace(m.orgInput.Value())),
+		renderStringFlag("--repos", strings.Join(splitCSVField(m.reposInput.Value()), ",")),
+		mapBoolToFlag(m.generate, "--generate"),
+		renderStringFlag("--voice", strings.TrimSpace(m.voiceInput.Value())),
+		renderStringFlag("--format", m.format),
+		mapBoolToFlag(m.dryRun, "--dry-run"),
+		mapBoolToFlag(m.wait, "--wait"),
+	}), " ")

+func (m dispatchTUIModel) View() string {
+	preview := m.preview()
+
+	leftWidth := max(m.width/2-2, 40)
+	rightWidth := max(m.width-leftWidth-6, 40)
+
+	left := m.renderFields(leftWidth)
+	right := m.renderPreview(preview, rightWidth)
+
+	header := "DISPATCH"
+	if m.styles.title.String() != "" {
+		header = m.styles.title.Render(header)
+	}
+	footer := m.renderFooter()
+
+	body := lipgloss.JoinHorizontal(lipgloss.Top, left, "  ", right)
+	return strings.Join([]string{header, body, footer}, "\n\n")

+
+func (m dispatchTUIModel) renderFields(width int) string {
+	rows := []string{
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldSource, "Mode", m.sourceMode.label()),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldSince, "Since", m.sinceInput.View()),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldUntil, "Until", m.untilInput.View()),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldBranchScope, "Branch scope", m.branchMode.label()),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldBranches, "Branches", m.branchesInput.View()),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldOrg, "Org", m.orgInput.View()),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldRepos, "Repos", m.reposInput.View()),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldGenerate, "Generate", boolLabel(m.generate)),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldVoice, "Voice", m.voiceInput.View()),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldFormat, "Format", m.format),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldDryRun, "Dry run", boolLabel(m.dryRun)),
+		m.renderField(dispatchTUIFieldWait, "Wait", boolLabel(m.wait)),
+	}
+
+	content := strings.Join(rows, "\n")
+	if m.styles.border.String() != "" {
+		return m.styles.border.Width(width).Render(content)
+	}
+	return content
+}

+func (m dispatchTUIModel) renderField(field dispatchTUIField, label string, value string) string {
+	prefix := "  "
+	if m.focusIndex == field {
+		prefix = "› "
+	}
+	line := fmt.Sprintf("%s%s: %s", prefix, label, value)
+	if m.focusIndex == field && m.styles.selected.String() != "" {
+		return m.styles.selected.Render(line)
+	}
+	return line
+}
+
+func (m dispatchTUIModel) renderPreview(preview dispatchTUIPreview, width int) string {
+	lines := []string{
+		"Preview",
+		fmt.Sprintf("Mode: %s", preview.EffectiveMode),
+		fmt.Sprintf("Scope: %s", preview.EffectiveScope),
+		fmt.Sprintf("Branches: %s", preview.EffectiveBranches),
+	}
+	if preview.ValidationError != "" {
+		message := "Error: " + preview.ValidationError
+		if m.styles.errorStyle.String() != "" {
+			message = m.styles.errorStyle.Render(message)
+		}
+		lines = append(lines, message)
+	}
+	command := preview.Command
+	if m.styles.previewCode.String() != "" {
+		command = m.styles.previewCode.Render(command)
+	}
+	lines = append(lines, "", "Command", command)
+
+	content := strings.Join(lines, "\n")
+	if m.styles.border.String() != "" {
+		return m.styles.border.Width(width).Render(content)
+	}
+	return content
+}

+func (m dispatchTUIModel) renderFooter() string {
+	mode := "navigate"
+	if m.interaction == dispatchTUIInteractionEdit {
+		mode = "edit"
+	}
+	return fmt.Sprintf("mode: %s   tab move   enter edit/apply   space toggle   r run   q quit", mode)

+	if m == dispatchTUISourceModeLocal {
+		return "local"
+	}
+	return "server"

+func (m dispatchTUIBranchMode) label() string {
+	switch m {
+	case dispatchTUIBranchModeAll:
+		return "all"
+	case dispatchTUIBranchModeCustom:
+		return "custom"
+	default:
+		return "default"
+	}
+}
+
+func boolLabel(value bool) string {
+	if value {
+		return "yes"
+	}
+	return "no"
+}
+
+func splitCSVField(value string) []string {
+	if strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
+		return nil
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(value, ",")
+	result := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
+	for _, part := range parts {
+		part = strings.TrimSpace(part)
+		if part != "" {
+			result = append(result, part)
+		}
+	}
+	return result
+}
+
+func compactStrings(values []string) []string {
+	result := make([]string, 0, len(values))
+	for _, value := range values {
+		if value != "" {
+			result = append(result, value)
+		}
+	}
+	return result
+}
+
+func mapBoolToFlag(enabled bool, flag string) string {
+	if enabled {
+		return flag
+	}
+	return ""
+}
+
+func renderStringFlag(name string, value string) string {
+	if value == "" {
+		return ""
+	}
+	return name + " " + quoteShellValue(value)
+}
+
+func quoteShellValue(value string) string {
+	if value == "" {
+		return `""`
+	}
+	if strings.ContainsAny(value, " ,:\t") {
+		return fmt.Sprintf("%q", value)
+	}
+	return value
+}
+
+func buildDispatchCommand(opts dispatchpkg.Options) string {
+	branchesValue := ""
+	if opts.AllBranches {
+		branchesValue = "all"
+	} else if len(opts.Branches) > 0 {
+		branchesValue = strings.Join(opts.Branches, ",")
+	}
+
+	return strings.Join(compactStrings([]string{
+		"entire dispatch",
+		mapBoolToFlag(opts.Mode == dispatchpkg.ModeLocal, "--local"),
+		renderStringFlag("--since", strings.TrimSpace(opts.Since)),
+		renderStringFlag("--until", strings.TrimSpace(opts.Until)),
+		renderStringFlag("--branches", branchesValue),
+		renderStringFlag("--repos", strings.Join(opts.RepoPaths, ",")),
+		renderStringFlag("--org", strings.TrimSpace(opts.Org)),
+		mapBoolToFlag(opts.Generate, "--generate"),
+		renderStringFlag("--voice", strings.TrimSpace(opts.Voice)),
+		renderStringFlag("--format", strings.TrimSpace(opts.Format)),
+		mapBoolToFlag(opts.DryRun, "--dry-run"),
+		mapBoolToFlag(opts.Wait, "--wait"),
+	}), " ")
+}

+func runDispatchTUI(cmd *cobra.Command) (dispatchpkg.Options, error) {
+	styles := newStatusStyles(cmd.OutOrStdout())
+	model := newDispatchTUIModel(styles, func() (string, error) {
+		return GetCurrentBranch(cmd.Context())
+	})
+	program := tea.NewProgram(model, tea.WithAltScreen())
+	finalModel, err := program.Run()
+	if err != nil {
+		return dispatchpkg.Options{}, fmt.Errorf("dispatch TUI failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	result, ok := finalModel.(dispatchTUIModel)
+	if !ok {
+		return dispatchpkg.Options{}, fmt.Errorf("dispatch TUI returned unexpected model %T", finalModel)
+	}
+	if result.cancelled || !result.submitted {
+		fmt.Fprintln(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "dispatch cancelled.")
+		return dispatchpkg.Options{}, errDispatchCancelled
+	}
+	return result.submittedOpts, nil
+}

I have the direction now: remove `--dry-run` and strip the CLI’s stored-dispatch semantics. I’m laying out the implementation options so we can lock the contract before edits.

Recommended approach: make the CLI contract explicitly inline-only.

1. Minimal compatibility layer.
Keep the existing request/response structs mostly intact, stop printing `web_url`, and ignore `id`/fingerprint fields.
Tradeoff: fast, but the CLI types still imply storage and the code keeps dead semantics around.

2. Inline-only cleanup. Recommended.
Remove `--dry-run`, delete stored-resource fields from the in-memory `Dispatch` type and top-level command flow, and narrow the server response model to the fields the CLI still uses for one-off output.
Tradeoff: a slightly broader edit, but the code matches the new product decision and stops teaching the wrong contract.

3. Server-only behavioral shim.
Leave the CLI surface mostly unchanged and rely on the backend to stop persisting while still returning a compatible shape.
Tradeoff: least local churn, but the CLI remains misleading and tests keep asserting the old model.

Design section 1, contract:
- `entire dispatch` becomes a one-off generation command in both local and server modes.
- `--dry-run` is removed from flags, parsing, wizard state, and tests.
- The CLI no longer exposes or prints stored-resource concepts like `id`, `web_url`, `fingerprint_hash`, or `deduped`.
- Rendered output remains the same for text/markdown/json except that JSON no longer includes those stored-resource fields.

Root cause is clear: local dispatch’s default “current branch” filter is too literal. It matches checkpoint metadata branch names exactly, so checkpoints created on `entire-dispatch` disappear after copying/renaming the worktree branch to `entire-dispatch-codex`, even though those commits are still on your current HEAD history.

Recommended approach:
1. Default-only reachability fallback. Recommended.
When local dispatch is using the implicit current-branch default, include checkpoints whose `Entire-Checkpoint` commit is reachable from `HEAD`, even if the stored branch name differs. Keep explicit `--branches ...` and `--branches all` behavior unchanged.
Tradeoff: fixes the worktree/renamed-branch bug without weakening explicit filters.

2. Always use reachability for local branch filtering.
Ignore stored branch names entirely in local mode and decide membership by commit reachability.
Tradeoff: more intuitive for copied branches, but changes explicit branch semantics more broadly.

3. Match both current branch name and checkpoint metadata branch aliases.
Try exact branch match first, then also allow likely source branches.
Tradeoff: heuristic and fragile.

+# Dispatch Local Current-Branch Reachability Design
+
+## Goal
+
+Make local `entire dispatch` treat the implicit "current branch" default as checkpoints reachable from the current `HEAD`, rather than requiring exact equality with stored checkpoint branch metadata.
+
+## Problem
+
+Local dispatch currently defaults to filtering checkpoints by the literal current branch name. That fails when a worktree branch has been copied or renamed, because committed checkpoint metadata keeps the original branch label. In this repo, checkpoints recorded under `entire-dispatch` disappear when running local dispatch from `entire-dispatch-codex`, even though the checkpoint commits are still on the current branch history.
+
+## Decision
+
+Only change the implicit current-branch default in local mode.
+
+- If the user explicitly passes `--branches`, keep exact branch-name filtering.
+- If the user passes `--branches all`, keep existing behavior.
+- If local dispatch falls back to the implicit current-branch default, include checkpoints whose `Entire-Checkpoint` commit is reachable from the current `HEAD`.
+
+This keeps explicit filters precise while making the default behavior match user expectations and the existing `entire explain` mental model.
+
+## Implementation Shape
+
+- Add a small `ImplicitCurrentBranch` signal to dispatch options.
+- Set it only when `resolveDispatchOptions` injects the current branch because the user did not provide `--branches`.
+- In local repo enumeration, use HEAD reachability instead of `summary.Branch` equality when `ImplicitCurrentBranch` is true.
+- Reuse the checkpoint trailer linkage to determine whether a checkpoint commit is reachable from the current branch.
+
+## Verification
+
+- Add a regression test where:
+  - checkpoint metadata branch is `entire-dispatch`
+  - current branch is `entire-dispatch-codex`
+  - no explicit `--branches`
+  - expected: checkpoint is included
+- Add a second test proving explicit `--branches entire-dispatch-codex` still excludes that checkpoint.
+- Run `go test ./cmd/entire/cli ./cmd/entire/cli/dispatch`
*** End Patch

content.text: from form remove until, generate prose, remove the custom file path option. how to handle organization, repos and branches in a better way. list selection would be ideal

I’m reworking the dispatch form shape: remove `Until`, remove `Generate prose?`, and remove custom voice input. I’m checking what `huh` field types we already use in this repo so I can suggest a list-based scope/branch flow that matches the existing CLI patterns instead of bolting on more free-text fields.

For the list-based version, should the form load real choices dynamically from the current repo context, or do you want static choice modes with a manual fallback?

My recommendation is dynamic:
- `Organization`: a select only when server mode is chosen and orgs can be discovered
- `Repos`: a multi-select of local repo paths when local mode is chosen
- `Branches`: a multi-select populated from git branches in the selected repo context

That gives the best UX, but it means the wizard needs to query git and possibly org context before rendering each list.
yes

Design section 1:

- Remove these fields from the wizard:
  - `Until`
  - `Generate prose?`
  - custom voice/file-path mode
- Keep only shipped voice presets:
  - `neutral`
  - `marvin`
- Keep time window as presets only:
  - `1 day`
  - `7 days`
  - `14 days`
  - `30 days`

Design section 2, scope flow:
- First field: `Dispatch mode`
  - `Local`
  - `Server`
- Second field becomes `Scope type`
  - in local mode: `Current repo` or `Selected repos`
  - in server mode: `Current repo` or `Organization`
- If `Selected repos` is chosen, show a `huh.MultiSelect[string]` of discovered local repos.
- If `Organization` is chosen, show a `huh.Select[string]` or `huh.MultiSelect[string]` depending on what the backend can actually enumerate cheaply. If we can only support one org cleanly, use a single select.

Design section 3, branches:
- Replace free-text branches with list selection.
- Branch selector should depend on scope:
  - `Current repo`: load local git branches for that repo
  - `Selected repos`: either
    - use `All branches` / `Current branch` only, or
    - compute the intersection of branch names across selected repos
- My recommendation:
  - for single-repo scopes, use a branch mode select plus optional branch multi-select
  - for multi-repo scopes, allow only `Current branch` or `All branches`
- That avoids a bad UI where users pick branch names that only exist in some repos.

Recommended UX:
1. `Mode`
2. `Scope type`
3. Scope picker list
4. `Branch mode`
5. Optional branch multi-select only when the scope is effectively single-repo
6. `Time window`
7. `Voice preset`
8. `Format`
9. `Wait`
10. Confirm

That keeps the form list-driven and removes the weakest text inputs. Does that shape look right?
yes

Design section 4, implementation boundaries:

- The wizard should gather real choices before building the form:
  - discover current repo
  - discover available local repos for selection
  - discover branches for the relevant repo scope
- Keep `resolveDispatchOptions(...)` as the final authority for turning wizard choices into CLI options.
- But the wizard should stop serializing list choices back into comma-separated text fields internally. It should hold structured state:
  - `selectedRepos []string`
  - `selectedBranches []string`
  - `scopeType string`
  - `branchMode string`
  - `voicePreset string`
- `buildDispatchCommand(...)` should still render standard flags, but only from the resolved structured options.

Testing:
- add wizard-state tests for:
  - local current repo defaults
  - selected repos mode requiring local mode
  - server organization mode
  - single-repo branch multi-select
  - multi-repo scope suppressing custom branch picking
  - voice preset command rendering with no custom voice path
- keep existing CLI option-resolution tests intact

If you want, I’ll implement this next.
yes
The form redesign is approved. I’m documenting the final shape first, then I’ll do a test-first pass around the wizard state and dynamic scope/branch choices before changing the UI code.

+# Dispatch List-Driven Wizard Design
+
+## Goal
+
+Replace the remaining weak free-text inputs in the `dispatch` wizard with structured list-based selection, while simplifying the form down to the options users actually want.
+
+## Changes
+
+- Remove `Until` from the wizard.
+- Remove `Generate prose?` from the wizard.

+- Keep only preset voice choices: `neutral`, `marvin`.

+## Scope UX
+
+The wizard should stop making users type scope by hand.
+
+- First choose `Mode`: `Local` or `Server`.
+- Then choose `Scope`:
+  - local: `Current repo` or `Selected repos`
+  - server: `Current repo` or `Organization`
+- `Selected repos` uses a multi-select list of discovered local repos.
+- `Organization` uses a single-select list of discovered org choices.

+  - `All branches`

+  - `Current branch`
+  - `All branches`
+
+This avoids invalid selections where a chosen branch exists in some repos but not others.
+

+
+The wizard should hold structured state instead of CSV text fields.
+
+- `scopeType`
+- `selectedRepos []string`
+- `selectedBranches []string`
+- `branchMode`
+- `voicePreset`
+
+The final command preview should still render standard CLI flags from resolved `dispatch.Options`.

The dispatch wizard is now list-driven and stripped down in [dispatch_wizard.go](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_wizard.go:1). I removed `Until`, removed the `Generate prose?` field, and removed custom voice/file-path input. The wizard now uses preset-only time windows, preset-only voices (`neutral`, `marvin`), and structured selection state for scope, repos, orgs, and branches.

Scope and branches are handled through dynamic `huh` selects now:
- mode defaults to `Local`
- scope is a list: `Current repo`, `Selected repos`, or `Organization` depending on mode and discovered choices
- repos use a multi-select of discovered sibling git repos/worktrees
- branches use list selection, and multi-repo scopes suppress custom branch picking in favor of `Current branch` or `All branches`

I also added the design note and plan in [2026-04-17-dispatch-list-driven-wizard-design.md](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/docs/plans/2026-04-17-dispatch-list-driven-wizard-design.md:1) and [2026-04-17-dispatch-list-driven-wizard.md](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/docs/plans/2026-04-17-dispatch-list-driven-wizard.md:1), and rewrote the wizard tests in [dispatch_wizard_test.go](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_wizard_test.go:1).

I’m checking the `huh` layout we’re generating so I can fix the spacing at the field level instead of guessing with random style tweaks. First I’m inspecting how the wizard groups the always-visible selects and multi-selects, because the screenshot suggests we’re rendering inactive fields that should probably be skipped or split into separate groups.

Yes. The spacing looks wrong because the form is still rendering the inactive fields instead of actually hiding them.

In `huh`, the built-in `Select` and `MultiSelect` fields don’t conditionally skip themselves, so even when `Repos` or `Organization` are “not used,” they still take vertical space. That’s why you get those big dead gaps.

Recommended fix:
- make the wizard conditional by page/group, not by always-visible fields with “used only when…” descriptions
- keep `Mode` and `Scope` first
- then show only the relevant picker:
  - local + current repo: no extra scope field
  - local + selected repos: show only repo multi-select
  - server + organization: show only org select

That will remove the empty spacing and make the form read like a real flow instead of one long sheet.

If you want, I’ll implement that next.

The bug was stale wizard state, not repo loading. In server mode the form was still carrying `Selected repos` internally after a mode switch, even though server dispatch only supports `Current repo` or `Organization`. I fixed that in [dispatch_wizard.go](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_wizard.go:1) by coercing server mode back to valid scopes only, and added coverage in [dispatch_wizard_test.go](/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli/entire-dispatch-codex/cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_wizard_test.go:1).

So now:
- `Local` supports `Current repo` and `Selected repos`
- `Server` supports `Current repo` and `Organization`

If you switch to `Server`, the wizard will no longer try to keep or act on `Selected repos`.

Verification:
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli -run 'Test(NewDispatchWizardState_|DispatchWizardState_|DispatchWizardChoices_|BuildDispatch)' -v`
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli ./cmd/entire/cli/dispatch`

If you want server dispatch to support repo selection too, that’s a separate product/contract change. Right now the CLI itself still enforces `--repos requires --local`.

I think this should be simplified. if doing local then you can only select different branches in current repo. should be multi select with the current branch already selected. if serever mode then you can select multiple repos. make sure repo name has org in front and it defaults to the default branch

I’m using `brainstorming` first because this changes the dispatch contract and wizard flow, not just a label. I’m checking the current wizard and parser together so the next pass simplifies both instead of only masking the UI.

One important clarification before I redesign it: should this simplification change the actual CLI contract too, so `entire dispatch --repos ...` works in server mode outside the wizard, or do you want this to be wizard-only while the raw flags keep `--repos` local-only?
cli contract

Recommended contract change:

1. Keep dual scope models.
- `--local`: only current repo, optional `--branches`, default current branch.
- server: allow `--repos org/repo,org/repo2`, default each repo to its default branch when `--branches` is omitted.
- keep `--org` as a separate server-only shortcut for “all repos in org”.
This matches what you asked without removing org-wide dispatch.

2. Remove repo scope from local entirely.
- local mode ignores or rejects `--repos`
- the wizard becomes simpler: local only asks for branches in the current repo
- server owns repo selection

3. Unify everything under `--repos`.
- no `--org`
- org-wide dispatch would require expanding repos client-side first
This is simpler on paper, but it removes a useful shortcut and adds more server lookup work.

Recommendation: `1`.

Concrete behavior:
- `entire dispatch --local`
  uses current repo only, current branch preselected
- `entire dispatch --local --branches main,release`
  dispatches those branches in the current repo only
- `entire dispatch --repos entireio/cli,entireio/entire.io`
  server dispatch across those repos, default branches if no `--branches`
- `entire dispatch --org entireio`
  server dispatch across accessible repos in that org, default branches unless `--branches all` or explicit branches is given

Does that contract look right so far, especially keeping `--org` as a separate server-only shortcut?
yes

Design section 1, CLI semantics:

- `--repos` becomes server-only, not local-only.
- `--local` is limited to the current repo.
- In local mode:
  - no repo picker
  - no `--repos`
  - branches are the only scope control
  - default branch selection is the current branch
- In server mode:
  - `--repos` accepts repo slugs like `entireio/cli`
  - omitted branches mean “default branch per repo”
  - explicit `--branches` still applies across selected repos
- `--org` remains as the server shortcut for org-wide dispatch.

Parser changes:
- replace the current `--repos requires --local` rule with:
  - `--repos` and `--org` remain mutually exclusive
  - `--repos` is invalid with `--local`
- default-branch behavior for server repo selection should not materialize branch names client-side; it should remain “no branches specified” so the backend/local dispatcher can use its default-branch path.

Does that section look right?
yes

Design section 2, wizard simplification:

- First field stays `Dispatch mode`:
  - `Local`
  - `Server`
- Local path:
  - no scope selector at all
  - branch multi-select from current repo branches
  - current branch preselected
  - label should make it clear this is “Current repo branches”
- Server path:
  - scope selector:
    - `Selected repos`
    - `Organization`
  - `Selected repos` uses a multi-select of repo slugs formatted `org/repo`
  - `Organization` uses the org picker
  - branch control defaults to `Default branches`
  - optional branch override can still allow `All branches` or selected branch names when that makes sense
- Repo labels in the wizard should always show `org/repo`, not bare repo names.

Recommended simplification for server branches:
- `Default branches` (default)
- `All branches`
- `Selected branches`

That keeps the local and server mental models clean:
- local = current repo, selected branches
- server = selected repos/org, default branches unless overridden

yes

docs/security-and-privacy.md:3:Entire stores AI session transcripts and metadata in your git repository. This document explains what data is stored, how sensitive content is protected, and how to configure additional safeguards.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:9:When you use Entire with an AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI), session transcripts, user prompts, and checkpoint metadata are committed to a dedicated branch in your git repository (`entire/checkpoints/v1`). This branch is separate from your working branches, your code commits stay clean, but it lives in the same repository.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:13:Anyone with access to your repository can view the transcript data on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. This includes the full prompt/response history and session metadata. Note that transcripts capture all tool interactions — including file contents, MCP server calls, and other data exchanged during the session.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:15:If your repository is **public**, this data is visible to the entire internet.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:30:- **Use a private repository.** This is the simplest and most complete protection. Transcripts on `entire/checkpoints/v1` are only visible to collaborators.

specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md:63:| `--dry-run` | off | Show what checkpoints, labels, warnings, and counts a real run would produce, without persisting anything or spending LLM tokens. Works with or without `--generate`. **Analysis fetches still happen** (they're cheap, cached per-checkpoint, and required for the preview to show real pending/failed/unknown/access-denied counts). What dry-run actually suppresses: LLM synthesis, persistence to the dispatches table, fingerprint reservation, and dedupe. In default mode, `dry_run: true` in the POST body instructs the server to skip those persistence-/cost-bearing steps and return the preview-shaped response; in `--local` mode, the CLI does the same work locally and skips the LLM call. |

+# Dispatch Remove Wait Design
+
+## Goal
+
+Remove `wait` from `entire dispatch` completely so dispatches always skip pending analyses instead of optionally blocking for them.
+
+## Contract Change
+
+- Delete the `--wait` flag from the CLI.
+- Delete the wizard field for waiting on pending analyses.
+- Delete `Wait` from `dispatch.Options`.
+- Delete `wait` from the cloud request payload.
+- Delete local waiting behavior before analysis fetches.
+
+After this change, dispatch always behaves like the current non-waiting path:
+
+- pending or generating analyses are skipped
+- warnings report the skipped count
+- no polling or blocking occurs
+
+## Scope
+
+This is a full contract removal, not just a UI cleanup.
+
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch.go`
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_wizard.go`
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/dispatch.go`
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/cloud.go`
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/server.go`
+- `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/local.go`
+- related tests
+
+## Behavior
+
+- Local mode should fetch analyses once and proceed with the existing pending-warning path.
+- Server mode should stop sending any wait hint to the backend.
+- Rendered warnings remain, but should no longer tell users to use `--wait`.
+
+## Verification
+
+- Add or update tests proving:
+  - the `dispatch` command no longer exposes `--wait`
+  - the wizard command preview does not emit `--wait`
+  - server/cloud request payloads do not include `wait`
+  - local dispatch still reports pending analyses without waiting
+- Run the full `cmd/entire/cli` and `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch` test suites.
